title: Send email
$idempotencyComment: `idempotent` rather than `unsafe-to-replay`, and the distinction is the point: without a key a retry sends a SECOND email, which is embarrassing and recoverable, where a retried payment is neither. Declaring the header anyway removes even that -- the generated executor derives the key from the RUN and the NODE, never fresh, so a resumed durable run mails nobody twice.

requireOneOf.error: needs an "html" or "text" body — an empty email is never intended
requireOneOf.$comment: Resend rejects this too, three frames later and in its own words. A node that knows its own requirement should say so before the round trip. This is the first cross-field requirement in the vocabulary: `required` is per-field and cannot express "one of these two".

config.label: From
config.description: Must be an address on a domain you have verified with Resend. An unverified sender is refused at send time, not at setup.

config.label: To
config.description: One address, a comma-separated list, or an expression. Resend's simulator addresses (delivered@resend.dev, bounced@resend.dev) are LIVE sends that are billed and counted — they are not a sandbox.

send.$comment: Resend wants a JSON array, and an author holding one address, a pasted list, or an upstream array should not have to know which. `list` splits a string on the separator, trims, drops the blanks, and passes an array straight through.

config.label: Custom headers
config.description: Sent as the email's own headers. The usual use is a threading or reference id.

outputShape.description: Which estate this ran against. Resend has no sandbox, so: fake or live.
The connection id that was used.
Resend's id for the email (a UUID). Look the send up with it, or dedupe on it.
